title: Intrinsic presentation of the coefficient/site mate square
statement:
Intrinsic presentation of the coefficient/site mate square.

theorem intrinsicCoefficientSiteMate
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Finite A] [Finite B]
    (φ : A →+* B) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (J : Etale.DerivedCategoryModule (ULift.{u + 1, u} A) X) :
    (scalarExtensionFunctor φ Y).map
        ((intrinsicCoefficientSiteDirectImageComparison A f).app J) ≫
      (directImageScalarComparison φ f).app ((etaleOriginOpenComparison A X).obj J) ≫
      (directImageConstantPush B f).map ((intrinsicCoefficientSiteScalarIso φ X).hom.app J) =
    (intrinsicCoefficientSiteScalarIso φ Y).hom.app
        ((Etale.lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)) f).rightDerivedFunctor.obj J) ≫
      (etaleOriginOpenComparison B Y).map
        ((Etale.scalarMate (RingHom.ulift.{u + 1, u + 1, u, u} φ) f).app J) ≫
      (intrinsicCoefficientSiteDirectImageComparison B f).app
        ((Etale.scalarExtension (RingHom.ulift.{u + 1, u + 1, u, u} φ) X).obj J)

proof.text: Use the proved realizationRestrictionDirectImage: the realization unit is sectionwise bijective for finite coefficients, and substitution of the three unit/section normalization equations proves the ordinary restriction/direct-image square.

Use the proved scalarSheafPullbackIso_inverseMate for the ordinary scalar normalization. Transpose the ordinary realization square under geometric adjunctions. The unit-normalized geometric coordinate map identifies the resulting restriction/pullback square. Exact restriction and pullback descend the square termwise, with their localization factor isomorphisms. Transpose under scalar adjunctions: scalarPresentation is the prescribed uniqueness map. On flat-term K-flat models the inverse scalar mate preserves inserted tensor units, hence agrees with both the published Etale.scalarPullbackIso and intrinsic directImageScalarPullbackIso. Universal derived counits descend this equality. Paste the canonical etale/pro-etale inverse-image square, whose scalar cube has the same pure-tensor normalization. Explicitly, exact restriction of scalarExtensionRepresentative is the adjunction transpose of the ordinary cochain unit followed by the inverse restriction factor. The geometric representative is the derived/exact comparison followed by the exact-pullback factor. Naturality of these factors reduces the derived normalization equation to the ordinary scalar-unit mate equation; uniqueness on K-flat representatives identifies the published etale comparison.

Take geometric mates of the two equal scalar/site/pullback routes. Move the scalar presentation across the A-counit by naturality, use the A-site counit-mate equation, the preceding cube equality, and then the B-site mate equation. Both transposes coincide. Injectivity of the geometric adjunction Hom equivalence yields exactly the displayed equality, with the two canonical presentation boundaries. This is an equality before any boundedness restriction; no scalar mate is inverted.
